claims.text: Sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles exhibit active atomic diffusion that invalidates the sluggish-diffusion explanation.
Surface-energy gradients drive rapid thermal segregation of Au and Cu to the nanoparticle surface.
Surface segregation creates a concentration gradient that accelerates the outward diffusion of Au and Cu.
Outwardly diffusing Au and Cu subsequently evaporate from the nanoparticles.
The segregation and evaporation mechanism becomes dominant when thermal energy overcomes the activation barrier for surface diffusion.
The PLD-grown sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles initially form a kinetically stabilized FCC solid solution.
Au and Cu surface mobility is expected to become active above approximately 400 K.
Core-to-surface chemical-potential differences caused by surface-energy gradients override bulk configurational-entropy stabilization.
Au and Cu have sufficiently low surface energies to lower total nanoparticle free energy by segregating to the surface.
The relatively low melting points of Au and Cu favor their surface segregation in this quinary alloy.
The high surface-to-volume ratio below 10 nm amplifies surface-energy-driven segregation.
Au and Cu have sufficiently high vapor pressures at the relevant elevated temperatures to undergo selective evaporation.
Selective evaporation of Au and Cu causes a progressive loss of these elements and widens the nanoparticle size distribution.
Surface-driven diffusion and evaporation reshape elliptical or icosahedral particles into spheres to reduce surface area.
The segregation threshold is lower for icosahedral particles than for truncated-octahedral particles because icosahedra have a higher initial surface-energy driving force.
Depletion of Au and Cu destabilizes the FCC solid solution.
The proposed surface-driven mechanism is dominant below 10 nm and fails in particles larger than 20 nm or in bulk material, where bulk diffusion and entropy dominate.
Sluggish diffusion can occur in high-entropy alloy matrices.
Magnetic fluctuations can alter magnetic-entropy and internal-energy contributions in CoCrFeMnNi.
The silicon nitride substrate may influence surface-diffusion kinetics in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says reshaping occurs rather than the coalescence 'predicted by sluggish diffusion models,' whereas the baseline says the prevailing sluggish-diffusion hypothesis predicts stabilization against coalescence.
